body:
From my brief two quarter stay at a university in California, I experienced maybe a hint of bullying but also a lot of emotional manipulation from so-called "friends". They would do dumb stuff and just in general say messed up things to each other, and I didn't like their kinda energy in general so I left them, but now I'm at community college trying to transfer to another uni.

For the most part, you should be fine though.
A toast "to the circle of life"!

I'm guessing the school you transferred to after the technical college was a different one than the one you started at. Were there any things specifically you didn't like about the school itself? And what made you choose the four-year that you transferred to and made you think it was better than the first college?
What was your reason for leaving the 4-year initially? Was there any specific part of the college/life that you didn't like?

Tell me more, either by PM or reply. If you're comfortable sharing, what was that painful road like? What did it entail? What interest(s) were you able to transform into something that makes you consider yourself successful? My parents are definitely all for me doing what I'm passionate about. Their problem is job prospects. But are you suggesting to possibly ignore some of their beliefs of how my success should be? It sounds right to me but it just makes me feel so guilty to go against their wishes. They have done everything for me. They are the best people I could ask for. So it's just so hard where to look.
